summary: SPHEREx  PlanetKwa is a web application designed to make real NASA SPHEREx observations easier to explore, compare, and investigate. It retrieves astronomical data, processes FITS images, and prepares them for visualization, allowing users to examine different observation dates and spectral channels. With interactive comparison tools, users can identify potential changes, including variations in brightness or previously unnoticed objects. When users spot something worth investigating, they can select a region, add their observations, and generate a PDF report containing relevant astronomical data and their findings. PlanetKwa makes this process more accessible through an intuitive interface and a helpful FAQ section, allowing even users without extensive astronomical experience to explore real space observations. By turning complex astronomical data into an accessible exploration tool, PlanetKwa encourages curiosity, supports further investigation, and makes observing our changing universe easier.
details:
How PlanetKwa Works

PlanetKwa transforms real NASA SPHEREx observations into an accessible environment for astronomical exploration.

Users can select an astronomical target using celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) or choose from our list of test objects. The application retrieves available observations from NASA SPHEREx through IRSA and downloads the corresponding FITS files.

Our Python-based processing pipeline handles the astronomical image data, prepares images for visualization, and uses World Coordinate System (WCS) information and Reproject to align observations to a common coordinate grid. This makes it easier to compare images captured at different times and explore different spectral channels.

Users can examine observations through interactive comparison tools, including Blink Animation and a Slider. When they identify a potentially interesting change, they can select a region, add personal notes, and generate a PDF report containing relevant observation metadata and their findings.

Benefits and Intended Impact

PlanetKwa reduces the technical barrier to exploring astronomical observations. Instead of requiring users to work directly with complex FITS files and specialized software, it provides a visual and interactive way to investigate real space data.

Our goal is to make astronomical exploration more approachable, encourage curiosity, and help users document observations that may deserve further scientific investigation.

Technology and Tools

The project was developed primarily in Python. We used:

  • Astroquery to access astronomical data services.
  • Astropy for FITS handling, celestial coordinates, and WCS.
  • NumPy for numerical operations and image data processing.
  • Reproject to align observations to a common coordinate system.
  • Pillow for image processing and rendering.
  • NASA SPHEREx / IRSA as the source of real astronomical observations.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative aspect of PlanetKwa lies in combining astronomical data processing, interactive visualization, and observation reporting in one application.

Throughout development, we focused on making complex scientific data easier to understand without losing its astronomical context. We considered usability for beginners, the accuracy of coordinate alignment, the differences between observation dates and spectral channels, and the importance of preserving relevant metadata.

We also considered the limitations of visual comparison: differences between images can indicate potential changes, but they require further investigation before any scientific conclusions can be drawn.
